We’re dropping an episode from one of our favorite podcasts, Unexplainable from Vox. In it, host Sally Helm considers whether or not it’s ethical to kill lantern flies, an invasive species that has gained a foothold on the East Coast of the US.

In the episode Sally explores what we owe other living creatures, how squishing bugs changes us, and what we should do when there is not a single clear moral path.

snippet.description:
A GS Foundation That Doesn’t Leave Revision to Chance

One of the biggest challenges in UPSC preparation is not just completing the syllabus — it is remembering and revising what you studied months ago.

In this video, we explain how the LevelUp IAS GS Foundation Course for UPSC CSE 2028 builds a structured revision cycle into the preparation itself. Instead of leaving revision entirely to the aspirant, the program uses weekly, subject-wise, quarterly and six-monthly tests to repeatedly bring older topics back into preparation.

For example, after completing a subject like Polity, aspirants face a cumulative test covering the entire subject. As preparation progresses, older subjects are brought back through combined and larger tests, helping students revise the syllabus multiple times instead of studying a topic once and moving on.

The GS Foundation 2028 program is designed for UPSC beginners and combines structured GS preparation with Prelims & Mains tests, Current Affairs, Answer Writing, CSAT, Essay, dedicated mentorship and Interview preparation.

The idea is simple: complete the syllabus, keep revisiting it, test yourself repeatedly, and build long-term retention for UPSC CSE 2028.
